summary.headline: Sell a narrow, human-led cyber-hygiene service to UK SMEs; validate demand before building software.
summary.best_opportunity: Productized cyber-readiness and phishing-response setup for small UK businesses.
summary.why_now: The UK government’s 2025 survey found 43% of businesses experienced a breach or attack in the prior year; phishing remains the leading disruption. This supports a practical service, not proof of willingness to pay.

top_opportunities.name: SME cyber-hygiene setup and monthly check-in
top_opportunities.description: Fixed-scope MFA, backups, access review, incident contacts and staff phishing-response playbook; refer technical assurance beyond competence.
top_opportunities.why_now: DSIT’s 2025 survey reports 43% of businesses experienced a breach or attack; 85% of affected businesses cited phishing.
top_opportunities.buyer: UK professional-services firms, small agencies and local operators with 5–49 staff.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200–£800 for basic tools, insurance and outreach; avoid claiming certification.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly or quarterly maintenance and staff onboarding.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong: software engineer can automate checks and reporting; security expertise must be bounded.
risks: Trust and liability; avoid penetration testing or compliance guarantees without qualifications.
Survey reports incidents, not buyers’ willingness to pay; validate locally.
top_opportunities.verdict: Best first test: service-led, scoped tightly, with explicit security limits.

top_opportunities.name: Missed-enquiry capture and follow-up for local trades
top_opportunities.description: Install website/WhatsApp enquiry capture, instant acknowledgement and human follow-up reminders.
top_opportunities.why_now: Directly ties to leads and revenue; demand signal is local and must be tested through direct outreach.
top_opportunities.buyer: Plumbers, electricians and other appointment/quote-based trades.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£500 using existing low-cost hosting and messaging tools.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–2 weeks if sold as a paid setup.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong technical fit; requires sales and client support.
risks: Consent, privacy and messaging compliance require careful configuration.
top_opportunities.verdict: Fast cash potential; sell a measurable result, not generic AI.

top_opportunities.name: Invoice chasing and cash-collection workflow
top_opportunities.description: Configure invoice reminders, ageing dashboard and escalation workflow around a client’s accounting package.
top_opportunities.why_now: Late payment is a recurring UK SME pain, but no live late-payment source was verified in this run; interview first.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small B2B service firms with recurring overdue invoices.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly workflow support or per-client SaaS later.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good automation fit; needs accounting-tool integration knowledge.
risks: Avoid debt collection claims and mishandling financial data.
top_opportunities.verdict: Test as integration service before building a standalone product.

top_opportunities.name: Vertical AI admin automation for small firms
top_opportunities.description: Automate one repetitive intake-to-document workflow with human approval and an audit trail.
top_opportunities.why_now: Potential productivity value, but broad AI adoption evidence was not independently established here; sell a specific time-saving pilot.
top_opportunities.buyer: One chosen niche such as recruiters or property managers.
risks: Errors and sensitive data create operational and privacy risk.
Generic AI automation is crowded; niche access is the bottleneck.
top_opportunities.verdict: Only proceed after securing a design partner and measurable baseline.

top_opportunities.name: Local-business website care and conversion service
top_opportunities.description: Fixed-price refresh plus ongoing updates, uptime, backups and enquiry-flow improvements.
top_opportunities.why_now: Recurring maintenance is straightforward to deliver, but current demand signal is weak without customer interviews.
top_opportunities.buyer: Independent clinics, trades and local professional services with dated sites.
risks: Many low-cost providers and DIY website tools.
Scope creep and client acquisition can consume part-time capacity.
top_opportunities.verdict: Bundle a concrete conversion fix with maintenance; avoid commodity redesigns.

best_pick.name: SME cyber-hygiene setup and monthly check-in
best_pick.why_it_wins: A government survey supplies a credible problem signal, and a tightly scoped service can earn before software is built. Evidence does not establish willingness to pay.
validation_plan: Interview 10 local firms with 5–49 staff about their last phishing incident, current controls and who owns remediation.
Offer a paid, fixed-scope pilot to 3 firms; proceed only if at least one pays and delivery is within a day.
best_pick.first_offer: £250 fixed-scope baseline and action plan; quote monthly follow-up separately, with no certification or security guarantee.
best_pick.mvp: Checklist-driven assessment, secure client questionnaire, prioritised actions and follow-up report; no custom platform.
best_pick.do_today: Draft a one-page scope and contact 10 local businesses for discovery; use the cited survey as context, not a scare tactic.
